points.description: States that removing an electron decreases electron–electron repulsion among the remaining electrons (fewer electrons repel one another; less repulsion as electrons are removed). Accept equivalent wording that clearly refers to electron–electron repulsion.

Relates the decreased electron–electron repulsion to a lower (more negative) potential energy of the remaining electrons/system. Accept wording such as 'less repulsion lowers the potential energy' or equivalent.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if lower potential energy is mentioned but not explicitly linked to decreased electron–electron repulsion.

levels.says: Mentions that potential energy decreases/becomes more negative, but does not connect this to decreased electron–electron repulsion.

points.description: States that the third and fourth electrons experience the same core charge (same effective nuclear charge). Accept 'core charge does not change between the 3rd and 4th ionizations' or equivalent.

States that the third and fourth electrons are removed from the same n=3 shell and therefore have the same radius (same distance from the nucleus). Accept 'both are valence/3p electrons' only if it clearly means same shell and radius.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only the same n=3 shell or only the same radius/distance is stated.

levels.says: States only that the 3rd and 4th electrons are in the same n=3 shell, or only that they have the same radius/distance, but not both.

points.description: States that the fifth electron is removed from the n=2 shell and therefore feels a higher core charge (greater effective nuclear charge) than the third/fourth electrons. Accept 'core charge jumps because the electron comes from an inner shell' or equivalent.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only the n=2 shell or only the higher core charge is stated.

levels.says: States only that the 5th electron is in n=2, or only that it feels a higher core charge, without the other part.

points.description: States that the fifth electron is in the n=2 shell, which has a smaller radius (is closer to the nucleus) than n=3, so it is more strongly attracted. Accept 'smaller distance from nucleus' or 'inner shell' if it clearly means smaller radius.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only the n=2 shell or only the smaller radius/closer distance is stated.

levels.says: States only that the 5th electron is in n=2, or only that it has a smaller radius/is closer to the nucleus, without the other part.

points.description: Explains that ionization energy is the energy needed to remove an electron, i.e. to overcome the attractive potential energy and bring it to zero (or to infinity); therefore a lower/more negative potential energy means a larger ionization energy. Accept equivalent wording linking potential energy to the energy required for removal.
points.partial_credit: One mark for a vague or incomplete link between potential energy and ionization energy.

levels.says: Mentions that ionization energy relates to potential energy or to overcoming attraction, but does not clearly connect lower/more negative potential energy to a greater ionization energy.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all seven ideas in the model answer: decreased electron–electron repulsion, its link to lower potential energy, same core charge and radius for the 3rd/4th electrons, higher core charge and smaller radius for the 5th electron, and the potential-energy/ionization-energy relationship. Part marks are available on the combined shell/radius/core-charge points when only one half is present, and on the potential-energy/ionization-energy point when the link is vague. No marks for simply quoting the energies or saying 'more energy because it is harder to remove' without the repulsion/core-charge/radius reasoning.
